t.7.21.1: Having reflected thus, the foremost of brahmins, swift of stride, set off toward the abode of Yama to tell him what had happened.
t.7.21.2: There he saw the god Yama, with Agni placed before him, attending to the dispensation due to each living being, of whatever sort it was.
t.7.21.3: But Yama, seeing that the great sage Nārada had arrived there, offered him the guest-water as dharma prescribes and spoke to him as he sat at ease.
t.7.21.4: Is all well, O divine sage? Is dharma not perishing? What is the purpose of your coming, O you who are attended by gods and gandharvas?
t.7.21.5: Then the blessed sage Nārada spoke these words: "Let it be heard; I shall declare it, and let the proper course of action be carried out."
t.7.21.6: O King of the Ancestors, this night-roaming demon, Daśagrīva by name, is approaching to bring you, who are most difficult to conquer, under his control by his acts of valor.
t.7.21.7: For this reason I have come in haste, O lord. Yet what indeed will he do today to you, whose weapon is the rod?
t.7.21.8: Meanwhile, from afar, the divine aerial chariot of that rākṣasa was seen approaching, like the risen sun.
t.7.21.9: Making that whole region free of darkness with the radiance of his Puṣpaka, the mighty one drew near.
t.7.21.10: The mighty-armed Daśagrīva saw, here and there, living beings experiencing the fruits of their good deeds and of their evil deeds as well.
t.7.21.11: Then the mighty Rāvaṇa, by his valour and by sheer force, set free those who were being tormented on account of their own evil deeds.
t.7.21.12: As the departed spirits were being set free by the mighty rākṣasa, the guardians of the dead, greatly enraged, rushed upon the lord of the rākṣasas.
t.7.21.13: Those heroes, in their hundreds of thousands, showered the Puṣpaka with barbed darts, iron clubs, spears, mallets, javelins and lances.
t.7.21.14: Swiftly, like bees, they broke apart the seats, the mansions, and the platforms and coverings of that Puṣpaka.
t.7.21.16: Then those mighty ministers of Rāvaṇa fought as they pleased and to the utmost of their strength, and so did the ten-faced king himself.
t.7.21.15: That aerial chariot Puṣpaka, which had become an abode of the gods, though being battered in the battle, remained just as it was, indestructible by the power of Brahman.
t.7.21.17: But those ministers of the lord of the Rākṣasas, their limbs smeared with blood and struck by every kind of weapon, waged a mighty battle.
t.7.21.18: And in the battle the illustrious ones struck one another with their weapons, both the great army of Yama and the ministers of the Rākṣasa.
t.7.21.19: But leaving aside those ministers of the mighty Rākṣasa, they rushed upon Daśānana himself with showers of spears.
t.7.21.20: Then the foremost of the Rākṣasas, his limbs smeared with blood and his body battered by the blows, shone in his vimāna like an aśoka tree in full bloom.
t.7.21.21: By the power of his divine weapons, that mighty one hurled tridents, maces, darts, spears, javelins and arrows, clubs, rocks and trees.
t.7.21.23: And all of them, surrounding him as masses of clouds surround a mountain, left him unable to breathe with their bhindipālas and spears.
t.7.21.22: But they, a hundred thousand strong, cast aside all those and warded off that weapon, and struck the dreadful rākṣasa who stood alone.
t.7.21.25: Then, after a moment, the lord of the Rākṣasas, having regained consciousness, stood upon the earth, armed with bow and arrows, enraged like Antaka.
t.7.21.24: His armour stripped away, enraged and drenched with streams of blood, he abandoned the Puṣpaka and stood upon the earth.
t.7.21.26: Then, fixing the divine Pāśupata weapon upon his bow and saying to them, "Stand, stand!", he drew that bow.
t.7.21.28: Those soldiers of Vaivasvata, scorched by his fiery energy, fell in that battle like trees consumed by a forest fire.
t.7.21.27: That arrow, garlanded with flames and followed in battle by flesh-eating creatures, once released, rushed onward, reducing both shrubs and trees to ashes.
t.7.21.29: Then that rākṣasa of fearsome valor, together with his ministers, roared a mighty roar, as though making the earth tremble.
